title: Choose the look of MATH
question: Each sketch is the steps screen at 2x (320x240 on the calculator) solving 2sin²x − sin x − 1 = 0 with one step expanded. Keep the roll, take another card, or re-roll.

options.label: Chalkboard
options.lineage: the classroom board a worked solution is written on
options.thesis: Steps written out like the teacher's board, and whatever changed in each line is in yellow chalk.
options.viewport: Problem strip on top, boxed answer right under it, then the steps; each step shows its new part in yellow.
options.risk: Dark ground can look heavy on the CE's backlight if the green drifts toward black.

raised.raise: Yellow is reserved for what changed in a step and is never used anywhere else.
Nothing is labelled twice: no 'Step 3:' text, the position says it.
Three chalk values plus one yellow; every rule is a 1 px line.
Fixed caption size and a strict left edge for every expression.

options.label: Worked Example
options.lineage: the 'Example / Solution' boxes in IB maths textbooks
options.thesis: Every answer is set like a textbook worked example: numbered margin tabs and the result in a tinted box.
options.viewport: Teal 'Example' strip with the problem, tinted answer box, then numbered steps with a caption in the margin.
options.risk: Familiar: it is close to what a careful textbook already looks like.

options.label: Warm Cards
options.thesis: Each step is a soft card on a warm ground, and the one bright colour marks what a key can act on.
options.viewport: Problem and answer in a top card, steps as stacked cards, the selected one outlined in the action colour.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and reads like Photomath; holds clarity, loses on feeling like maths.
options.risk: Cards cost vertical space on a 240 px screen, so fewer steps fit.

options.label: Gate Board
options.thesis: Steps as board rows, the changed part lit until you notice it.
options.viewport: Rows of steps in a fixed column grid.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nothing about solving maths is travel.
options.kept: One colour reserved only for change.
options.risk: A costume of an airport on a maths tool.

options.label: Transit Line
options.thesis: Steps as stations on one line, sub-steps as a branch.
options.viewport: A vertical line with a station per step.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the line eats width the expressions need.
options.kept: Fixed label size and a strict alignment grid.
options.risk: Decoration that takes 30 px of a 320 px screen.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Steps as coded entries, decoded only when selected.
options.viewport: Black field with one white plot.
options.case: Fuses poorly: hiding captions behind codes defeats learning the method.

options.label: Centre Rail
options.thesis: Two text columns around a rail of keys.
options.case: Fuses poorly: 320 px has no room for twin columns.
options.kept: Three values only, every rule at one pixel.
options.risk: Too dense for a calculator screen.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.case: Fuses poorly: graphx cannot draw translucent layers and hatching reads as noise at this size.
options.kept: Tabular figures so numbers line up.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: White screen, black maths, one blue selection bar, like the TI-OS MathPrint screens.
canonCard.viewport: Title bar, steps as a plain list, blue bar on the selected step.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other TI program.
